note: Every README claim, machine-checked. bash scripts/verify.sh runs each command and prints PASS/FAIL; the CI claims job runs the same script on every push, so the README cannot drift from the code. Claims are read-only: they run tests and builds (gitignored artifacts only) and never rewrite committed files.

claims.claim: A shell redirect is a write, and only a real redirect: `echo pwned >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys` is file-edit, while `npm test 2>&1` and `npm test > /dev/null` stay test-run.
claims.command: $PYTHON -c "from sololicense.coding.actions import classify_command as c; assert c('echo pwned >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys').action_class == 'file-edit'; assert c('npm test 2>&1').action_class == 'test-run'; assert c('npm test > /dev/null').action_class == 'test-run'"

claims.claim: Force-pushing a protected branch is denied in both spellings (--force and the +refspec form); a plain push is not.
claims.command: $PYTHON -c "from sololicense.coding.actions import classify_command as c; assert c('git push --force origin main').hard_deny and c('git push origin +main').hard_deny and not c('git push origin main').hard_deny"

claims.claim: Verified runs promote a class up the ladder (full gate suite: decisions, promote, demote, restore).
The committed before/after benchmark evidence exists and parses.
The CLI produces the one-command self-install prompt for an agent.
